title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Zscaler
providers.scope_notes: Covers Zscaler (ZIA, ZPA, OneAPI via Authentication Service / ZIdentity). SaaS; OneAPI needs services linked to Authentication Service; legacy ZIA API needs an API subscription; Workflow Automation, Client Connector and ZDX API keys not covered.

controls.name: ZPA API key Status
controls.setting: Administration > API > Private Access API > Edit

controls.name: ZPA API key Role
controls.what: Predefined or custom role (e.g. API Read Only) enforces RBAC on ZPA API operations.

controls.name: Session Validity Interval
controls.setting: Add API Keys > Session Validity Interval

controls_unknown: Source-IP restriction for OneAPI clients, ZPA keys or legacy ZIA sessions (Admin Sign-On Policy and ZIA restricted admin access pages do not state API coverage)
Whether the Authentication Service Admin Sign-On Policy or MFA applies to legacy ZIA API password logins
Whether deleting/disabling a ZPA API key or ZIA authorization server ends already-issued bearer tokens
Whether API client create/delete and token revoke appear as named actions in Authentication Service audit logs (documented actions are generic Create/Update/Delete)
Whether read-only (GET) API calls are recorded in any audit log
Expiry of JWT key pairs (zscaler-2) and Sandbox tokens
OneAPI rate limits (only legacy limits fetched)

auth_paths.name: ZPA API key (client ID and client secret, legacy ZPA API)

authentication.summary: ZPA API key = client ID + secret, posted to https://config.private.zscaler.com/signin to get a bearer token for /mgmtconfig endpoints.

ip_restriction.boundary: Not documented for ZPA API keys.

lifetime.summary: Key itself has no documented expiry; session validity up to 3,600 s

renewal.summary: Call /signin again with the same client ID and secret.

administration.summary: Admins with full API Key Management access create keys with a status and RBAC role (e.g. API Read Only); keys can be edited, disabled or deleted. Authentication Service keys show read-only here.
administration.conditions: Keys created via Zscaler Deception cannot be edited or deleted here.

offboard.details: The key carries its own API role and is not tied to an admin user.

inventory.details: API Keys page (Administration > API > Private Access API) lists all keys with status, role and validity.

usage.ui: Zscaler Admin Console > Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Private Access; filter Client ID; Download for CSV

log_sources.name: ZPA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Records admin and API actions; Client ID column; 6-month retention.

credential_id_fields.notes: API key's client ID that made changes

anomaly_cues: Changes by an unfamiliar Client ID

containment.steps: Disable or delete the ZPA API key.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether issued tokens end before their validity interval (max 3,600 s).

calls.log_notes: ZPA audit action list includes Sign In
ZPA audit log documents changes and sign-ins, not reads
